
Read/Clean Merged Data and Load Libraries

```{r}

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(FSA)      
library(rstatix)
library(caret)
library(randomForest)

merged_data <- read.csv("merged_data.csv", header = TRUE)


# Kenny's Phase 2 Submission 

merged_data$SOVI_RATNG<-as.factor(merged_data$SOVI_RATNG) #cleaning
nri_cols<-names(merged_data)

length(unique(merged_data$STCOFIPS))==nrow(merged_data)

col_summary <- merged_data |> 
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ case_when(
    all(is.na(.x)) ~ "all_na",
    n_distinct(.x, na.rm = TRUE) == 1 ~ "one_value",
    TRUE ~ "ok"
  ))) |> 
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "status")

# Separate results
all_na_cols <- col_summary |> filter(status == "all_na") |> pull(column)
one_value_cols <- col_summary |> filter(status == "one_value") |> pull(column)

list(
  entirely_na = all_na_cols,
  one_unique_value = one_value_cols
)

mean(is.na(merged_data$CFLD_EVNTS))
mean(is.na(merged_data$ERQK_EVNTS))
mean(is.na(merged_data$WFIR_EVNTS))

table(merged_data$AVLN_EXPB) #208 counties with building avalanche dmg
table(merged_data$AVLN_EXPP) 
table(merged_data$AVLN_EXPPE) #population equivalence
table(merged_data$AVLN_EXPT)

merged_data[which(!is.na(merged_data$AVLN_EXPB)),]%>%select(COUNTY,STATE)

hist(merged_data$EAL_VALT)
hist(log(merged_data$EAL_VALT))

merged_data$log_EAL_VALT<-log(merged_data$EAL_VALT) #log since skewed
summary(merged_data$EAL_VALT)

#all skewed
hist(merged_data$EAL_VALA)
hist(merged_data$EAL_VALB)
hist(merged_data$EAL_VALPE)

summary(merged_data$EAL_VALA)
summary(merged_data$EAL_VALB)
summary(merged_data$EAL_VALPE)

merged_data$log_EAL_VALA<-log(merged_data$EAL_VALA+1)
merged_data$log_EAL_VALB<-log(merged_data$EAL_VALB)
merged_data$log_EAL_VALPE<-log(merged_data$EAL_VALPE)

merged_data%>%select(EAL_VALT,STATE,COUNTY)%>%arrange(desc(EAL_VALT))%>%head(10)

merged_data[which.max(merged_data$EAL_VALT),c("STATE","COUNTY")] #LA is the highest EAL_VALT

merged_data[which(merged_data$SOVI_RATNG=="Data Unavailable"),]%>%select(STATE,COUNTY,SOVI_SCORE)
#missing SOVI rating, American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands,Virgin Islands
#Also missing SOVI Score, obviously

summary(merged_data$SOVI_SCORE)
hist(merged_data$SOVI_SCORE)

merged_data_s<-filter(merged_data,SOVI_RATNG!="Data Unavailable") # Created "merged_data_s", removing the ten counties from territories that are missing SOVI data.


```

Phase 2 and 3

```{r}

### EAL_VALT: Expected Annual Loss (Total) ###

# Compare Mean and Median Values

summary_stats <- merged_data_s %>%
  group_by(SOVI_RATNG) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    Mean = mean(EAL_VALT, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(EAL_VALT, na.rm = TRUE))

print(summary_stats)


# Boxplot for EAL_VALT by SOVI_RATNG (Using the Original Scale)

ggplot(merged_data_s, aes(x = SOVI_RATNG, y = EAL_VALT, fill = SOVI_RATNG)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Expected Annual Loss (EAL_VALT) by Social Vulnerability Rating (SOVI_RATNG)",
    x = "Social Vulnerability Rating",
    y = "Total Expected Annual Loss (EAL_VALT, $)") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) + # Format Y-axis as dollar values
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), # Rotate x-axis labels
    legend.position = "none") + 
  geom_point(data = summary_stats, aes(y = Mean), shape = 23, fill = "white", size = 3) # To show the mean visually!


# Boxplot for EAL_VALT by SOVI_RATNG (Using a Log Transformation)

ggplot(merged_data_s, aes(x = SOVI_RATNG, y = EAL_VALT, fill = SOVI_RATNG)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Expected Annual Loss (EAL_VALT) by Social Vulnerability Rating (SOVI_RATNG)",
    x = "Social Vulnerability Rating",
    y = "Total Expected Annual Loss (EAL_VALT, $)") +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma) + # Format Y-axis as dollar values
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), # Rotate x-axis labels
    legend.position = "none") + 
  geom_point(data = summary_stats, aes(y = Mean), shape = 23, fill = "white", size = 3) # To show the mean visually!

# Post-Hoc Testing & Effect Sizes

kruskal_test(merged_data_s, EAL_VALT ~ SOVI_RATNG)

dunn_result <- dunnTest(EAL_VALT ~ SOVI_RATNG,
                        data = merged_data_s,
                        method = "bonferroni") # Dunn's test (with Bonferroni p-value adjustment)
dunn_result


merged_data_s %>% kruskal_effsize(EAL_VALT ~ SOVI_RATNG) # Effect Size is 0.0466 (SMALL)

# Manually Calculating Effect Size

# 1. Assuming your total clean sample size is stored as N
N <- nrow(merged_data_s) # Get the total number of counties (rows) used in the analysis

# 2. Assuming the dunnTest result is stored in 'dunn_result'
#    The results table is accessed via $res
dunn_results_table <- dunn_result$res

# 3. Calculate the effect size 'r' and add it to the table
dunn_results_with_r <- dunn_results_table %>%
  mutate(
    effect_size_r = abs(Z) / sqrt(N), # Calculate r using the Z-statistic and total N
    is_significant = P.adj < 0.05) # Add a column to flag significant results

dunn_results_with_r


```

```{r}

### HWAV_EALPE: Heat Wave - Population Loss ###
### Focus: Population loss from a hazard correlated with socioeconomic factors. Heat Wave loss is primarily driven by lack of air conditioning, age, and poverty

# Compare Mean and Median Values

summary_stats <- merged_data_s %>%
  group_by(SOVI_RATNG) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    Mean = mean(HWAV_EALPE, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(HWAV_EALPE, na.rm = TRUE))

print(summary_stats)


# Boxplot for HWAV_EALPE by SOVI_RATNG (Using the Original Scale)

ggplot(merged_data_s, aes(x = SOVI_RATNG, y = HWAV_EALPE, fill = SOVI_RATNG)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Population Loss due to Heat Wave (HWAV_EALPE) by Social Vulnerability Rating (SOVI_RATNG)",
    x = "Social Vulnerability Rating",

# Boxplot for EAL_VALT by SOVI_RATNG (Using a Log Transformation)

ggplot(merged_data_s, aes(x = SOVI_RATNG, y = HWAV_EALPE, fill = SOVI_RATNG)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Population Loss due to Heat Wave (HWAV_EALPE) by Social Vulnerability Rating (SOVI_RATNG)",
    x = "Social Vulnerability Rating",
    y = "Population Loss (HWAV_EALPE, $)") +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma) + # Format Y-axis as dollar values
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), # Rotate x-axis labels
    legend.position = "none") + 
  geom_point(data = summary_stats, aes(y = Mean), shape = 23, fill = "white", size = 3) # To show the mean visually!

# Post-Hoc Testing & Effect Sizes

kruskal_test(merged_data_s, HWAV_EALPE ~ SOVI_RATNG)

dunn_result <- dunnTest(HWAV_EALPE ~ SOVI_RATNG,
                        data = merged_data_s,
                        method = "bonferroni") # Dunn's test (with Bonferroni p-value adjustment)
dunn_result


merged_data_s %>% kruskal_effsize(HWAV_EALPE ~ SOVI_RATNG) # Effect Size is 0.0466 (SMALL)

# Manually Calculating Effect Size

# 1. Assuming your total clean sample size is stored as N

# 2. Assuming the dunnTest result is stored in 'dunn_result'
#    The results table is accessed via $res
dunn_results_table <- dunn_result$res

# 3. Calculate the effect size 'r' and add it to the table
dunn_results_with_r <- dunn_results_table %>%
  mutate(
    effect_size_r = abs(Z) / sqrt(N), # Calculate r using the Z-statistic and total N
    is_significant = P.adj < 0.05) # Add a column to flag significant results

dunn_results_with_r
```

```{r}

### CWAV_EALPE: Cold Wave - Population Loss ###

# Compare Mean and Median Values

summary_stats <- merged_data_s %>%
  group_by(SOVI_RATNG) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    Mean = mean(CWAV_EALPE, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(CWAV_EALPE, na.rm = TRUE))

print(summary_stats) # The most notable feature is the zero median loss for the Very High group. This is unsual and suggests that a large portion of Very High counties may not experince cold waves at all, or the loss is negligible. 


# Boxplot for CWAV_EALPE by SOVI_RATNG (Using the Original Scale)

ggplot(merged_data_s, aes(x = SOVI_RATNG, y = CWAV_EALPE, fill = SOVI_RATNG)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Population Loss due to Cold Wave (CWAV_EALPE) by Social Vulnerability Rating (SOVI_RATNG)",
    x = "Social Vulnerability Rating",
    y = "Population Annual Loss (CWAV_EALPE, $)") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) + # Format Y-axis as dollar values
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), # Rotate x-axis labels
    legend.position = "none") + 
  geom_point(data = summary_stats, aes(y = Mean), shape = 23, fill = "white", size = 3) # To show the mean visually!


# Boxplot for CWAV_EALPE by SOVI_RATNG (Using a Log Transformation)

ggplot(merged_data_s, aes(x = SOVI_RATNG, y = CWAV_EALPE, fill = SOVI_RATNG)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Population Loss due to Cold Wave (CWAV_EALPE) by Social Vulnerability Rating (SOVI_RATNG)",
    x = "Social Vulnerability Rating",
    y = "Population Loss (CWAV_EALPE, $)") +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma) + # Format Y-axis as dollar values
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), # Rotate x-axis labels
    legend.position = "none") + 
  geom_point(data = summary_stats, aes(y = Mean), shape = 23, fill = "white", size = 3) # To show the mean visually!

# Post-Hoc Testing & Effect Sizes

kruskal_test(merged_data_s, CWAV_EALPE ~ SOVI_RATNG) # p-value is statistically significant, which means there are significant differences between CWAV_EALPE and SOVI_RATING

dunn_result <- dunnTest(CWAV_EALPE ~ SOVI_RATNG,
                        data = merged_data_s,
                        method = "bonferroni") # Dunn's test (with Bonferroni p-value adjustment)
dunn_result


merged_data_s %>% kruskal_effsize(CWAV_EALPE ~ SOVI_RATNG) # Effect Size is 0.0936, which indicates that SOVI-RATING plays a larger role in CWAV_EALPE, compared to EAL_VALT and HWAV_EALPE

# Manually Calculating Effect Size

# 1. Assuming your total clean sample size is stored as N
N <- nrow(merged_data_s) # Get the total number of counties (rows) used in the analysis

# 2. Assuming the dunnTest result is stored in 'dunn_result'
#    The results table is accessed via $res
dunn_results_table <- dunn_result$res

# 3. Calculate the effect size 'r' and add it to the table
dunn_results_with_r <- dunn_results_table %>%
  mutate(
    effect_size_r = abs(Z) / sqrt(N), # Calculate r using the Z-statistic and total N
    is_significant = P.adj < 0.05) # Add a column to flag significant results

dunn_results_with_r # The differences are complex. For example, Relatively Low SOVIs are statistically different from Relatively High SOVIs. The Very Low group is not statistically different from the Relatively Low group. This suggests that SOVI is not simplr or linear for this hazard



```
